title: Tenant credit window skew causing sustained throttling in Dedicated topologies
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple Dedicated customers running bursty inference workloads experienced sustained 429 throttles and SLA flapping over a 36-hour window. Root cause analysis points to a drift between tenant credit windows maintained by the admission controller and the burst token reconciliation job; when the reconciliation lagged, tenants accumulated stale negative state that prevented recovery even after credits were available. Impact: production outages for two paying enterprise customers (reduced throughput and elevated latency), escalations to SRE and account teams, and temporary customer-promoted failovers to Hosted API.
comments: 2026-02-20 Aisha Patel: Ticket created after PagerDuty escalation from Enterprise Support. Initial triage indicates Dedicated-only impact; Hosted customers unaffected.

2026-02-20 Marco Ruiz: Reproduced locally by simulating burst windows misaligned by clock skew + delayed reconciliation job. Observed admission controller retaining stale negative token counts for tenants.

2026-02-21 Evelyn Chen: Added monitoring dashboard for tenant-credit-latency and reconciliation-lag. Short-term mitigation: manual rebuild of in-memory tenant credit state on affected Dedicated nodes.

2026-02-22 Marco Ruiz: Rolled out hotfix v2.3.1 to admission controller: (1) guard that rejects negative durable token snapshots older than 30s; (2) forward-compatible reconciliation backoff logic to avoid over-correcting. Canary rollout to 3 Dedicated pools.
2026-02-23 Customer Support (Rohit Mehra): Two customers reported improved throughput after hotfix; one still saw intermittent 429s during peak bursts.

2026-02-25 Marco Ruiz: Identified root cause in reconciliation job: batching window aggregated updates by epoch alias which could collapse two adjacent windows when the compaction timer fired late. Added deterministic ordering and a unit test covering epoch boundary cases.
2026-03-01 QA (Liam O'Connor): Extended integration test harness to run burst-simulation against Dedicated topologies in CI; added reproducible scenario used in postmortem.
2026-03-08 Aisha Patel: Postmortem draft linked (see PRD link: https://confluence.redwood/DED-cred-skew-pm); recommending follow-ups for monitoring, safeguards, and operator tooling.

2026-03-12 Marco Ruiz: Backfill migration script prepared to sanitize durable token stores for all Dedicated clusters. Scheduled rolling migration with per-cluster guardrails and automated rollback on increased 429s.
resolution: Partial mitigation deployed (v2.3.1) to admission controller and reconciliation job hardened. Full rollout pending sanitized durable store migration and expanded observability. No code path requires customer data changes.
next_steps: Complete rolling migration to sanitize durable token stores across all Dedicated clusters (owner: Marco Ruiz, ETA 2026-03-15)
Ship runtime-2.3.2 with reconciliation ordering fix and explicit epoch TTLs (owner: Engineering Release, ETA 2026-03-17)
Expand monitoring: add alerting for reconciliation-lag > 10s and tenant-credit-negative-counts, with runbook linking back to this ticket (owner: SRE, ETA 2026-03-14)
Customer communication: send unified incident summary and mitigation timeline to affected customers and AMs once migration is complete (owner: Support, ETA 2026-03-16)
